name: SSH + X11 Forwarding
description: Not a product — a built-in capability of OpenSSH (ssh -X) that tunnels individual X11 application windows over an encrypted SSH connection. Unlike everything else in this table, it doesn't mirror a whole desktop — it forwards one GUI app's window at a time, using raw X11 protocol traffic with no video compression.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: X11 forwarding is inherently for X11 protocol windows; native Wayland apps aren't compatible without an XWayland shim

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration; works over any reachable network, including a VPN like Tailscale

Open Source.comment: OpenSSH is fully open source (BSD-style license); the X11 protocol itself is also an open standard

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Forwards individual app windows, not a full multi-monitor desktop session

Microphone Passthrough.comment: No audio channel at all by default; audio would need a separate manual SSH tunnel (e.g. for PulseAudio)

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Optional generic SSH compression (-C flag) exists, but it's static, not adaptive to network conditions

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Multiple users can each SSH in independently and forward their own windows, but there's no shared/isolated desktop session concept

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: There's no image/video compression at all by default — it relays actual X11 drawing commands, which is lossless by nature

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Not video-based; performance is dominated by per-operation round-trip latency, not a frame rate

Pre-Login Access.comment: Requires already being authenticated over SSH to launch an app; it doesn't show the target's actual login/greeter screen

No Account Required.comment: Just needs SSH credentials (password or key) on the target machine, no cloud account of any kind

Shared Clipboard.comment: X11 selection (middle-click paste) works, but bridging with the client OS's native clipboard often needs extra tools/config

2FA / MFA.comment: Possible via SSH server-side PAM modules (e.g. TOTP), but not enabled or built-in by default

Windows: Host.comment: Windows doesn't run X11 apps natively; not a standard use case even via WSL

Windows: Client.comment: Needs a third-party X server installed (VcXsrv, Xming, or MobaXterm's built-in one) — nothing works out of the box

macOS: Host.comment: Not a standard workflow; would require manually installed X11 applications

macOS: Client.comment: Requires installing XQuartz separately; no longer bundled with macOS since 10.8

Linux X11: Host.comment: The native, defining use case — works out of the box on virtually any Linux distro

Linux: Client.comment: Works natively, no extra software needed on an X11-based Linux client

Android: Client.comment: Possible via Termux + a third-party X server app, but not an official/standard setup

Free Tier.comment: Entirely free; OpenSSH ships built into virtually every Linux/Unix/macOS system

Enterprise.comment: No product to license — it's a protocol capability, not a company or paid tier
